item.title: Pologne-Un homme arrêté après des menaces visant Tusk et le ministre de la Défense
item.description: La police polonaise a arrêté un homme soupçonné de préparer une attaque contre le Premier ministre Donald Tusk et le ministre de la Défense Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a annoncé dimanche le ministre de l'Intérieur.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La police polonaise a arrêté un homme soupçonné de préparer une attaque contre le Premier ministre Donald Tusk et le ministre de la Défense Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a annoncé dimanche le ministre de l'Intérieur. Marcin Kierwinski a précisé à la chaîne publique TVP Info que l'homme était âgé d'une soixantaine d'années et avait été interpellé dans la région de Basse-Silésie, dans le sud de la Pologne. "Les services de sécurité l'ont identifié grâce à une analyse détaillée de contenus publiés en ligne", a-t-il ajouté. Donald Tusk et Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, dans des messages publiés sur X, ont remercié la police pour sa réaction "rapide et déterminée". Si les crimes violents sont relativement rares en Pologne, le pays est profondément polarisé sur le plan politique et est confronté à des menaces sécuritaires en raison de sa proximité avec la guerre en Ukraine. En août, la police a interpellé un homme de 23 ans accusé d'avoir appelé à l'assassinat de hauts responsables politiques polonais. En 2024, Donald Tusk avait déclaré avoir reçu des menaces après une tentative d'assassinat du Premier ministre slovaque Robert Fico. Les autorités polonaises sont en état d'alerte après une série d'actes de violence dans des établissements scolaires qui a conduit à la mort d'un agent d'entretien jeudi.

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy tells ABC he will organize elections if Russia agrees to 60-day ceasefire
item.description: "Please tell Putin, give us two months," Zelenskiy told ABC's "This Week."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday in response to critical comments from US President Donald Trump that he will organize elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agrees to a 60-day ceasefire. "Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organize elections," Zelenskiy told ABC's "This Week." Trump on Saturday criticized Zelenskiy for attacking Russian oil refineries a day after the US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues to fund its war in Ukraine . "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump had told reporters at the White House. In response, Zelenskiy said "it's up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader and noted that Putin would also like to change who is leading Ukraine. He said it is easy for Ukraine to be blamed for higher fuel prices "when everybody in the world understands because of the war in (the) Middle East , the prices are rising." Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"ready to halt"] attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Under terms of the deal as described by Trump on Friday, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and global markets, equal to about 2.25 million barrels of fuel. The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day. Trump is under pressure to bring down rising fuel prices ahead of November midterm elections that will determine whether his Republican Party will retain control of the US Congress for his final two years in office. Many lawmakers, including Republicans, have criticized the diesel deal as rewarding Putin.

item.title: Verstappen cruises to first Singapore GP win as Antonelli closes on crown
item.description: It was Max Verstappen's first win in Singapore.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen delivered a commanding performance to win the Singapore Grand Prix from pole position on Sunday, securing his second straight victory of the season after a perfect weekend that included a [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"sprint race triumph"]. The Dutchman controlled the race from the start at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, fending off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who finished second while Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was third to close in on a first title. Verstappen, who won the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, had never won in Singapore before and he had come into the race weekend stating he had "unfinished business". "It's taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre, even though I think the medium tyre for everyone was more of a struggle," Verstappen said. "But it worked out, so of course very happy to win here... The last two races have been really positive for us and it's just great to see." Antonelli extended his championship lead over teammate George Russell to 102 points and the Italian can mathematically win the title in the next round in Austin. "Can I? Really?" a surprised Antonelli said when he was told after his 14th podium of the season. "Well, let's not worry about that. Let's try to do the best weekend as possible and finish the job." Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had qualified third on the grid but he endured a torrid evening, slipping to sixth behind Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri after the two McLaren drivers overtook him in the dying stages as he struggled with his tyres. Russell, who started at the back of the grid due to engine penalties, finished ninth behind Liam Lawson and Nico Hulkenberg while Isack Hadjar - who also started at the back - was 10th. VERSTAPPEN SHUTS THE DOOR Leclerc reacted faster than polesitter Verstappen at the start, nearly lining up alongside the Dutchman heading into turn one, but the Red Bull driver veered to the left to shut the door on the Ferrari and retain his lead. As the race progressed, Verstappen steadily pulled clear on soft tyres, with Red Bull urging him to manage their life as Ferrari threatened an undercut. Hamilton's struggles became apparent early as he lost pace on medium tyres in third place and Ferrari brought him in for softs before Leclerc pitted on lap 25 in a move timed to emerge ahead of his teammate. Hamilton's frustration boiled over on team radio as he urged Ferrari to let him past Leclerc, saying: "I need to use this speed, mate," before Leclerc responded by setting the fastest lap. When Verstappen finally pitted on lap 33, his commanding lead allowed him to rejoin in first place. Lance Stroll's retirement with clutch issues triggered another VSC period that sparked a flurry of pit stops and Russell's timing proved unfortunate as the VSC ended earlier than expected, dropping him to 10th. RADIO ISSUES FOR VERSTAPPEN The strategy chaos benefited Leclerc, who caught and passed Hamilton on lap 46 to claim second place, though he remained nearly 15 seconds behind Verstappen, who faced radio communication problems for the second time this weekend. The issue forced his engineer to resort to coded messages, asking the Dutchman to key his mic to make a sound or stay silent when given options on strategy. The final stint saw Hamilton's pace collapse as multiple drivers closed in sensing a podium. Norris attempted to pass Hamilton on lap 54, but the Ferrari left the track and went wide while the McLaren went on the dirty part of the track, allowing Antonelli to overtake and move up to fourth. Antonelli then passed Hamilton for third before Norris found his opportunity at turn 10. Hamilton's misery was completed when Piastri overtook him on the final lap, relegating the Ferrari driver to sixth place.

item.title: Volkswagen CEO says transformation is 'shared responsibility' in appeal to EU
item.description: In his speech at the Paris auto show, Oliver Blume backed proposed "Made in Europe" rules and welcomed an EU-China deal that could cut Chinese imports of plug-in hybrid vehicles to the bloc by more than half.
item.dc:creator: Rachel More
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen chief Oliver Blume expects European policymakers to create the framework needed to make the German automaker's restructuring a success, he said on Sunday, amid a push by Brussels to shield industry from low-cost Chinese competitors. At an event titled "For Europe" on the eve of the Paris motor show, Blume said Volkswagen was working to reduce complexity across the company, whose brands range from mass-market VW to high-end marques like Porsche and Lamborghini, in what he called "the biggest transformation programme in our history". "This is a shared responsibility: The business community must become more competitive and create attractive opportunities, while policymakers must establish the right framework conditions," he said. PRICE WAR IN ELECTRIC VEHICLES The auto show in Paris comes at a critical juncture for Europe's top carmaker, which is undergoing a major restructuring and is racing to update its mass-market electric vehicle offering as Chinese competitors rapidly gain ground in Europe. Battered by an EV price war and falling sales at home, Chinese automakers are aggressively expanding into Europe. In his speech, Blume backed proposed "Made in Europe" rules to incentivise local manufacturing, and welcomed [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"a deal"] between the EU and China that could cut Chinese imports of plug-in hybrid vehicles to the bloc by more than half. "Those who sell here should compete under comparable conditions and create jobs and value here in Europe too," Blume said at the event, attended by France's minister for industry Sebastien Martin. Battling to implement sweeping job cuts and threatening to close up to four plants in Germany, Blume also faces pressure from investors to prove his [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"turnaround strategy"] goes beyond downsizing to make strides in product development and software. A suite of affordable EVs across Volkswagen's volume brands, including VW, Spain's Cupra and the Czech Republic's Skoda, will be on show at the event. Volkswagen will also premiere its new ID. Tiguan electric SUV. Volkswagen is by far Europe's top-selling automaker, with a consistent market share of roughly a quarter over the last decade, even as Chinese entrants like BYD (002594.SZ) and Leapmotor (9863.HK) build a following. Still, Volkswagen is feeling the heat. Its CEO is among German auto industry leaders [USN:L8N44O0MW TEXT:"calling for"] a more protectionist EU stance, as fears of retaliation from Beijing give way to worries that brutal competition in China has spread to Europe. EUROPEAN MARKET 'COULD BECOME VERY UNPROFITABLE' Gregor Williams, an analyst at Rhodium Group, said: "Industry has become a lot more concerned about the competitive challenge arising in China." The downturn in China's domestic auto market is creating export pressure, Williams said. "It's one thing to lose revenues," he added. "But if China also manages to export the price war, the European market could become very unprofitable."

item.title: Nuevo ataque contra aeropuerto de Riad provoca incendio, un día después de otro en que murieron 12
item.description: La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen dijo que un "proyectil no identificado" había impactado el domingo en el aeropuerto internacional de Riad, provocando un incendio, pocas horas después de que los hutíes, respaldados por Irán, advirtieron a las compañías aéreas y a los viajeros que se mantuvieran alejados de los aeropuertos sauditas .
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen dijo que un "proyectil no identificado" había impactado el domingo en el aeropuerto internacional de Riad, provocando un incendio, pocas horas después de que los hutíes, respaldados por Irán, advirtieron a las compañías aéreas y a los viajeros que se mantuvieran alejados de los aeropuertos sauditas . La coalición también dijo que las defensas aéreas sauditas habían interceptado un misil de crucero en las inmediaciones del Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid. No se facilitaron más detalles de inmediato. El aeropuerto permanece cerrado tras el ataque del sábado, en el que murieron 12 personas y más de 300 resultaron heridas, el ataque más mortífero de este tipo contra el reino en más de una década, en un contexto de una escalada de los combates entre los hutíes y las fuerzas gubernamentales yemeníes. A pesar del cierre temporal del aeropuerto, el Ministerio de Energía saudita dijo que una conferencia internacional sobre energía, prevista desde hacía tiempo, seguiría celebrándose en Riad el domingo. La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen informó de que el proyectil del domingo tenía como objetivo la Terminal 4 del aeropuerto, sin dar más detalles. "Reiteramos nuestra advertencia a todas las compañías aéreas, expertos, empleados, trabajadores y viajeros para que no usen los aeropuertos ni el espacio aéreo sauditas, ya que son vulnerables a los ataques y se han convertido en un teatro de operaciones para nuestras fuerzas, con la excepción de los aeropuertos de (las ciudades santas de) La Meca y Medina", habían dicho antes los hutíes en una publicación en X. Arabia Saudita ha intensificado su intervención militar en Yemen en las últimas semanas, lanzando ataques contra los hutíes y respaldando una contraofensiva del Gobierno yemení después de que el grupo respaldado por Irán se hizo con territorio estratégico en la costa del mar Rojo el mes pasado. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Yemen, controlado por los hutíes, dijo el domingo que cualquier nueva acción militar saudita en Yemen provocaría una respuesta más contundente, y añadió que sus acciones se regirían por el principio de reciprocidad.

item.title: Sheinbaum pide a poblaciones costeras de México refugiarse ante cercanía de huracán Simón
item.description: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, instó a los residentes de las poblaciones de la costa del Pacífico mexicano a permanecer bajo techo este domingo mientras el poderoso huracán Simón, de categoría 4, se acercaba a tierra, amenazando con vientos destructivos, peligrosas marejadas ciclónicas e inundaciones potencialmente mortales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, instó a los residentes de las poblaciones de la costa del Pacífico mexicano a permanecer bajo techo este domingo mientras el poderoso huracán Simón, de categoría 4, se acercaba a tierra, amenazando con vientos destructivos, peligrosas marejadas ciclónicas e inundaciones potencialmente mortales. Simón se encontraba a unos 105 km al oeste-noroeste de la ciudad portuaria Manzanillo, en el estado Colima, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 230 km/h, según informó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (CNH) de Estados Unidos en su último boletín de las 9:00 hora local (1500 GMT). El huracán se desplazaba hacia el nor-noroeste a 11 km/h, con su centro situado a unos 140 km al sur-sureste de Cabo Corrientes, en el vecino estado de Jalisco. "Ante el próximo impacto del huracán Simón categoría 4, exhortamos a la población de municipios costeros de Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit y Michoacán a mantenerse en resguardo hasta el aviso oficial de que el peligro ha terminado", dijo Sheinbaum en una publicación en X. La mandataria indicó que continuaban las evacuaciones preventivas hacia zonas más seguras y exhortó a la población a no salir a la calle y a seguir las instrucciones de Protección Civil. El CNH informó que Simón podría tocar tierra entre Playa Perula y Cabo Corrientes en las próximas 12 a 18 horas, aunque un cambio en su trayectoria proyectada hacia el oeste planteaba la posibilidad de que el centro de la tormenta permaneciera en alta mar. Incluso sin tocar tierra directamente, era probable que se registraran vientos catastróficos y marejadas ciclónicas que amenazaran vidas a lo largo de partes de la costa centro-occidental de México, advirtió la agencia. Las autoridades mexicanas han declarado el nivel máximo de alerta en 28 municipios de Jalisco y Colima, mientras que otros 93 municipios se encuentran bajo alerta alta, según informes de medios locales. El aeropuerto internacional de la localidad turística Puerto Vallarta ha cerrado temporalmente, al tiempo que las autoridades han suspendido actividades no esenciales y habilitado refugios de emergencia en las comunidades costeras amenazadas. El CNH advirtió que las fuertes lluvias previstas hasta el lunes podrían provocar inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra potencialmente mortales, especialmente en zonas montañosas. Simón se intensificó rápidamente hasta convertirse en un huracán de categoría 4 el sábado, lo que llevó a las autoridades a desplegar personal militar, equipos de emergencia y brigadas de protección civil en las comunidades costeras vulnerables. "SE INUNDÓ TODA LA CASA" El sábado en Manzanillo, una ciudad portuaria clave, los residentes se mostraban mayormente tranquilos a pesar de la tormenta que se aproximaba, sin señales evidentes de compras de pánico en los supermercados. Algunos comercios habían comenzado a proteger sus escaparates con tablones, mientras los negocios cerraban y las calles permanecían relativamente vacías. El personal de Protección Civil había clausurado las playas, instalado barreras y colocado banderas de advertencia rojas y negras, instando a los habitantes a mantenerse alejados de la costa. Durante la noche y la madrugada, Simon se desvió de su trayectoria directa hacia tierra firme, evitando parte de los daños previstos, aunque aun así trajo lluvias y vientos que provocaron inundaciones y desperfectos en Manzanillo. Se desplegaron efectivos policiales y militares por toda la ciudad. Hacia el final de la mañana del domingo, cuando parecía haber pasado lo peor de la tormenta, los residentes comenzaron a retirar el agua que, según relataron, había empezado a inundar sus hogares de madrugada. En el barrio de La Alameda, una zona en el sur de la ciudad, los vecinos caminaban con dificultad entre aguas que les llegaban a las espinillas, mientras miembros del Ejército, junto con las familias, sacaban con cubos el agua de las viviendas hacia la calle. “Las camas, los refrigeradores, las estufas, todos los muebles se mojaron, se inundó toda la casa”, dijo a Reuters Cecilia Palomar, a las puertas de su hogar. “Mi mamá no quiere salir, la llevamos con mi hermano, a lo más alto. Es una señora ya mayor, pero no quiere salir. No quiere estar lejos de su casa”. María Elena Vázquez relató que su casa comenzó a llenarse de agua hacia las cinco de la mañana y no escondió su malestar por los sucedido. "(Estamos) mal, muy mal, y con enfermos", afirmó. La tormenta llega una semana después de que el huracán Polo azotara la península mexicana Baja California como huracán de categoría 2, derribando árboles y postes de tendido eléctrico e inundando calles.

item.title: Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
item.description: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. "Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained." "The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days." A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking. "Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. "When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said. LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well. "I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement. "The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added. The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health. The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health. Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17. Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

item.title: At least 139 migrants dead, including some children, after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
item.description: At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday. The boat, carrying 305 people, capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of October 8-9, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts. Around 82 people survived the shipwreck, the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Photographs shared by the UN agency showed worn-out sandals and sneakers washed up on the shore. "Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac. "This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said. Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased. The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment. The migrants were heading to Yemen, with the hope of eventually making it to wealthier Gulf nations, even as Yemeni nationals themselves [USN:L6N45E0CP TEXT:"flee their country"], which is [USN:L6N45T0PU TEXT:"experiencing"] the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce in 2022. "Despite the violence in Yemen, migrants are still making the perilous journeys hoping to make it to the Gulf countries," the IOM statement said. FIGHTING IN ETHIOPIA Fighting has also broken out in Ethiopia since last month in the [USN:L6N45W02E TEXT:"biggest escalation of violence"] since the 2020-2022 Tigray war. An IOM official told Reuters that the UN agency had documented heavy migrant traffic along the so-called Eastern Route through Djibouti for several years. "People continue to use the route amid changing conditions in Ethiopia and Yemen, although the volume and direction of movement can shift over time," the official said. Ethiopian migrants interviewed as part of the agency's most recent situation report on Djibouti from September 20 to September 30 said they had left their country due to difficult living conditions, including the impact of drought. "Some migrants also reported that they were fleeing conflict and forced recruitment by armed forces," the report said. Multiple residents of Tigray, where fighting erupted on September 23, have told Reuters that they had seen Tigrayan rebels forcibly recruit young men into the defence forces. The rebels have denied conducting forced recruitment. The conflict has sparked fears of a return to all-out war with Ethiopia and Eritrea severing relations over alleged Eritrean support for the rebel alliance seeking to overthrow Ethiopia's government. Eritrea has denied backing the alliance. SEVERE RISKS The so-called Eastern Route presents many dangers, including accidents at sea, trafficking and arbitrary arrests once on land. In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route, according to IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, as the number of people undertaking the journey increased by 18%. IOM has described the crisis sparked by the fighting in Yemen as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the agency last week. More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, it said.

item.title: Saudi Arabia reports injuries in new attack at Riyadh airport, day after strike kills 13
item.description: The attack comes a day after the deadliest strike on the kingdom in more than a decade killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 at the airport.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari, Yasmine Ghania
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday. Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. An unspecified number of people were injured, the Saudi civil aviation authority said, adding it was still assessing the damage. The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. It later added that a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis, who are fighting a ground war in Yemen against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government. The airport has been closed since Saturday's attack, although a long-planned international energy conference went ahead in Riyadh on Sunday as planned. HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and said the group had attacked the airport in Dammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) . The Saudi government's media office and Aramco did not respond to requests for comment. The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed the strike on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport late on Sunday, adding that "damage assessments and safety inspections of airport facilities are under way." An eyewitness aboard a taxiing aircraft at the Dammam airport told Reuters that around 8:30 p.m. (1730 GMT) on Sunday, they saw a projectile strike the tarmac beside several parked aircraft, causing a fire. The witness said the aircraft returned to the gate, where passengers disembarked and were told to leave the airport. Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed several delays and cancellations on Sunday evening for arrivals and departures at Dammam airport, which serves the capital of the oil-producing region and is the kingdom’s third-largest airport. The Houthis earlier on Sunday had renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers and travellers against using Saudi airports. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said. 'WORSE IS YET TO COME,' HOUTHIS WARN Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month. The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours, including against the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada. Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity. "Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD A five-day conference of international energy organization WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre about 10 km (6 miles) from the Riyadh airport, the Saudi energy ministry said. A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory from the ministry. No further details were immediately available and it was not clear which ministers joined the meeting. Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting the event, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link. German officials were trying to organise a return flight for economy minister katherina Reiche, who was in Riyadh to attend the WPC conference and ministers' meeting. She was supposed to return to Berlin on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely that her flight would not be able to take off due to the airport's closure, and alternatives were being considered. Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes at all schools in Riyadh would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff. In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the dead included four Saudis and two Bangladeshis, as well as nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said. India's embassy in Riyadh said on Sunday one of its citizens injured in the attack had died, adding to the initial death toll of 12. Four people were killed in the two previous attacks on the airport earlier in the week. One of the attacks also caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

item.title: Smith sets catching record as Australia take firm grip on test
item.description: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side finished the third day of the first test with a 139-run lead over hosts South Africa before bad light brought an early close to Sunday's play at Kingsmead.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side finished the third day of the first test with a 139-run lead over hosts South Africa before bad light brought an early close to Sunday's play at Kingsmead. Smith took four superb catches to take his test tally to 223, going past the record of 220 held by England's Joe Root. Two of the catches showed outstanding anticipation as Smith shuffled across a few steps to snag South Africa captain Temba Bavuma and Kyle Verreynne as they both tried reverse sweeps off the spin bowling of Nathan Lyon. He also produced a flying dive across first slip to break the record and see off the threat of David Bedingham. His last catch, off Beau Webster, brought South Africa’s innings to a close as they scored 284 in reply to Australia’s first innings of 390. At stumps, Australia were 33 without loss in their second innings with Nic Maddinson 17 not out and Travis Head scoring 10. Smith’s heroics were in contrast to his last test appearance in South Africa eight years ago when he was captain of the team embroiled in a ball-tampering scandal and handed a one-year ban. But the sparse home crowd on Sunday were reminded of the 37-year-old’s skills as he contributed to his side’s handy lead with some extraordinary athleticism. South Africa face an uphill battle if they are to salvage something from the test with two days’ play remaining. Their batsmen were guilty of playing loose shots at crucial junctures after resuming the day 27-1 with three wickets falling before lunch, four more in the second session but the last two adding 87 runs before the innings came to a close. "Every time we looked like getting something going, we lost a wicket and that set us back a bit," said South Africa batting coach Ashwell Prince. Bedingham top scored with 49 but, like most of his teammates, got out to a rash shot. His was a thick edge off a back-foot drive to a Pat Cummins delivery that saw Smith dive across first slip like a top goalkeeper to snag the ball. Other batting contributions came from Aiden Markram, who made 37, and tail-enders Simon Harmer (35 not out) and Keshav Maharaj with 34. Cummins returned figures of 3-54, with two wickets each for Josh Hazlewood, Mitch Starc and Lyon. "There is still a long way to go but we hope that in the South African second innings, the pitch will deteriorate," said Lyon, whose spin could prove key to the outcome of the game. All three days of the test have ended early because of bad light stopping play, and extra time will again be added to all three of Monday's sessions.

item.title: Ukraine-Trump annonce un cessez-le-feu dans l'énergie, Zelensky attend des précisions
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et son entrée en vigueur, avant d'être rapidement contredit par son homologue ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et son entrée en vigueur, avant d'être rapidement contredit par son homologue ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky. "Avec effet immédiat, il y a un CESSEZ-LE-FEU ÉNERGÉTIQUE dans la guerre entre la Russie et l'Ukraine. Les deux parties ont donné leur accord. Ne le violez pas !", a écrit Donald Trump sur son réseau Truth Social. Quelques minutes plus tard, Volodimir Zelensky a cependant indiqué ne pas avoir été informé d'une telle trêve, déclarant au site d'information Axios que l'annonce du président américain constituait "une surprise" pour lui. "L'Ukraine soutient le cessez-le-feu, et il est important que la Russie le soutienne également. Nous attendons des précisions de la partie américaine", a-t-il écrit par la suite sur l'application Telegram. "Pour sa part, l'Ukraine soutient toujours PLEINEMENT les mesures visant à la désescalade, à la protection des vies humaines et aux décisions nécessaires pour mettre fin à la guerre et garantir une paix durable." Moscou n'a pas commenté les annonces de Donald Trump dans l'immédiat. Plus tôt, Volodimir Zelensky s'était dit disposé à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cessait ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses assauts. Il a également déclaré qu'il organiserait des élections en Ukraine si le président russe Vladimir Poutine acceptait un cessez-le-feu global de 60 jours. Samedi, Donald Trump a imputé la hausse des prix du diesel aux États-Unis aux frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes et a déclaré que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement", ajoutant que l'Ukraine devrait le remplacer à sa tête car il avait laissé passer plusieurs occasions de conclure un accord avec Moscou. "DITES À POUTINE DE NOUS DONNER DEUX MOIS" La forte hausse des prix mondiaux du diesel, qui a suivi le déclenchement de la guerre avec l'Iran en février, est devenue un handicap politique pour le Parti républicain de Donald Trump à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat du mois prochain, lors desquelles les démocrates pourraient reprendre le contrôle d'une ou des deux chambres du Congrès. Volodimir Zelensky a réaffirmé dimanche la position de longue date de l'Ukraine, selon laquelle elle est disposée à cesser ses attaques contre les raffineries russes uniquement dans le cadre d'une désescalade réciproque du conflit, qui exigerait que Moscou mette également fin à ses frappes contre les infrastructures électriques ukrainiennes. Tout accord de ce type devrait s'accompagner de "garanties réelles", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. "La véritable cause de la guerre en Europe, c'est la Russie et la Russie seule", a-t-il dit, sans faire directement référence aux propos de Donald Trump. "Il est possible de mettre fin aux frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques dès aujourd'hui, mais Vladimir Poutine ne le veut pas." "Dites à Poutine de nous donner deux mois, 60 jours de cessez-le-feu total, 60 jours, et nous organiserons des élections", a également déclaré Volodimir Zelensky à la chaîne américaine ABC. Samedi, il a réagi avec colère à l'annonce par Donald Trump d'un accord d'approvisionnement en diesel avec la Russie, estimant que celui-ci encouragerait les attaques de Moscou contre l'Ukraine. "UNE TRAHISON" Des analystes ont déclaré que l'accord conclu par Donald Trump avec Moscou avait peu de chances d'entraîner une baisse durable des prix des carburants, les volumes concernés restant bien inférieurs aux exportations habituelles de la Russie lorsque ses raffineries ne sont pas visées par des attaques. L'accord sur le diesel a également été critiqué par des élus américains, dont le représentant républicain Don Bacon, qui a estimé qu'il était temps de renforcer les sanctions plutôt que de les alléger. Dans les rues de Kyiv, plusieurs habitants ont fait part de leur colère après la suggestion de Donald Trump selon laquelle l'Ukraine devrait se trouver un nouveau dirigeant prêt à conclure un accord avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine. "Personne n'a le droit de nous dire ce que nous devons faire, d'autant que des élections ne peuvent pas être organisées en temps de guerre", a déclaré Sabina, une institutrice de 40 ans, en référence à l'interdiction des élections en Ukraine sous le régime de la loi martiale pour des raisons de sécurité. "À mes yeux, c'est une trahison de la part de nos partenaires", a-t-elle déclaré au sujet des remarques de Donald Trump. Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré qu'il poursuivrait dimanche ses discussions avec les dirigeants européens et que des échanges avaient lieu quotidiennement sur des dispositifs supplémentaires de défense aérienne, notamment des munitions pour les avions de combat utilisés pour abattre les drones russes à réaction. Lundi, le ministre ukrainien des Affaires étrangères, Andrii Sybiha, doit participer à une réunion du Conseil des affaires étrangères de l'Union européenne qui devrait examiner un renforcement de la pression des sanctions contre la Russie ainsi que l'avancement des négociations sur l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Union européenne.

item.title: Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire with Russia, surprising Zelenskiy
item.description: There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump made a surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday that he said was "effective immediately", but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal. There was no word from Moscow on the ceasefire announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries. He blames those strikes for a rise in diesel prices that is hurting his Republican Party ahead of US midterm elections next month. In a dramatic deterioration in relations, Trump on Saturday warned Zelenskiy that he had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""] attacking Russian refineries, and urged Ukrainians to replace their leader at new elections. Trump said Zelenskiy had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow. In a post on his Truth Social platform on Sunday, Trump unexpectedly announced that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, but did not elaborate further. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote. RISING GLOBAL FUEL PRICES Trump, whose war in Iran has been widely blamed for hiking global fuel prices, had previously announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine in [USN:FWN4560K2 TEXT:"mid-September"], although neither side ever confirmed that such an agreement had been reached. A person familiar with the situation said the US had threatened to cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine as well as weapons procurement under the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) system, as it pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian energy sites. The [USN:L1N45X056 TEXT:"US threats"] were earlier reported by the Financial Times. The person added that Zelenskiy was speaking to European leaders about de-escalating the situation with Trump. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Zelenskiy said he had discussed Trump's ceasefire announcement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb. "Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side," he said on Telegram. Speaking in his nightly video address, Zelenskiy said [USN:L1N45X05G TEXT:"Russian forces"] were still launching air attacks on energy infrastructure, including a strike on a joint heating and power plant in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. A Ukrainian official confirmed the attack had taken place after Trump's announcement of the ceasefire. Hours earlier, Zelenskiy had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, repeating his long-standing position that he was willing to do so only if President Vladimir Putin suspended Russian strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure. PROMISE OF ELECTIONS Trump also called for elections in Ukraine, suspended since the 2022 Russian invasion, to which Zelenskiy responded that he would call a vote if Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire. Zelenskiy said it was "up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader, but added that there needed to be an end to the fighting first. Ukrainian law [USN:L1N44G089 TEXT:"prohibits elections under martial law"] for security reasons. "Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskiy said. The Ukrainian leader rejected that he was to blame for energy price rises, adding that "everybody in the world" knew that the war in the Middle East was a bigger factor. The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of the midterms, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress. On Saturday, Zelenskiy responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine and cost more lives. Under terms of the deal as described by Trump on Friday, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and global markets, equal to about 2.25 million barrels of fuel. The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day. Several US lawmakers also criticised the diesel deal. US Senator Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, [USN:L1N45X03S TEXT:"said"] the diesel supply deal with Russia may be illegal and will put American lives at risk. On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin. "No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher. "In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks. Ukrainian officials reported [USN:L1N45X05T TEXT:"new Russian attacks"] on Sunday, killing three people outside a grocery store in Kharkiv and three in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk. Moldova, on Ukraine's western border, reported a new incursion by what officials said were Russian drones, landing only about 35 km (22 miles) from the capital Chisinau.

item.title: L'Arabie saoudite annonce des blessés dans une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport de Ryad
item.description: Les autorités saoudiennes ont fait état de blessés lors d'une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport international de Ryad survenue dimanche, au lendemain d'un assaut contre ce même aéroport, revendiqué par les Houthis, qui a fait 13 morts.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Les autorités saoudiennes ont fait état de blessés lors d'une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport international de Ryad survenue dimanche, au lendemain d'un assaut contre ce même aéroport, revendiqué par les Houthis, qui a fait 13 morts. Selon la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen, un "projectile non identifié" a frappé dimanche le terminal 4 de l'aéroport international du roi Khaled, provoquant un incendie. Un nombre indéterminé de personnes a été blessé, a indiqué l'autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile, ajoutant que l'étendue des dégâts était encore en cours d'évaluation. La coalition a également indiqué que les défenses aériennes saoudiennes avaient intercepté un missile de croisière à proximité de l'aéroport. Le porte-parole militaire des Houthis, Yahya Saree, a déclaré dans un discours diffusé dimanche à la télévision que le groupe allié de l'Iran revendiquait l'attaque de samedi et avait également visé l'aéroport de Dammam, dans la province saoudienne bordée par le golfe Persique, ainsi que deux installations du géant pétrolier saoudien Saudi Aramco. L'Autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile a confirmé que l'aéroport de Dammam avait été visé par une attaque dimanche. En début de journée, les Houthis avaient renouvelé leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, déclarant qu'ils demeuraient des cibles potentielles d'opérations militaires et appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés, tout en prévenant que Ryad porterait la responsabilité de toute interception qui échouerait. L'Arabie saoudite a renforcé son engagement militaire au Yémen ces dernières semaines, menant des frappes contre les Houthis et soutenant une contre-offensive des forces gouvernementales après que le groupe s'est emparé le mois dernier de secteurs stratégiques le long de la côte de la mer Rouge. Les Houthis ont également déclaré dimanche que l'Arabie saoudite avait mené 124 frappes aériennes au Yémen au cours des dernières 24 heures, notamment contre Sanaa et le bastion du groupe à Saada. TRUMP N'A PAS EXCLU D'INTERVENIR Le ministère yéménite des Affaires étrangères contrôlé par les Houthis a dit que toute nouvelle action militaire saoudienne au Yémen entraînerait une riposte de plus grande ampleur, ajoutant que ses actions seraient guidées par le principe de réciprocité. "Tant que l'ennemi saoudien ne mettra pas fin à son agression et à son ingérence au Yémen, le pire est à venir, si Dieu le veut", a déclaré le ministère dans des communiqués relayés par la chaîne Al Masirah, contrôlée par les Houthis. Le président Donald Trump a déclaré samedi que les États-Unis envisageaient de participer aux frappes saoudiennes contre les Houthis dans ce conflit, qui constitue une extension de la guerre contre l'Iran déclenchée en février par Washington et Israël. Ces nouvelles menaces interviennent alors que l'Arabie saoudite a maintenu l'accueil d'un important congrès international de l'énergie à Ryad, dans un centre situé à environ 10 kilomètres de l'aéroport. En parallèle, une réunion ministérielle du Forum international de l'énergie s'est également tenue dimanche. Alors que sa séance plénière devait se dérouler à huis clos, selon une note destinée aux médias, aucune autre précision n'était disponible dans l'immédiat et on ignorait quels ministres participaient effectivement à la réunion. Par ailleurs, les autorités saoudiennes ont informé les parents que l'accueil des élèves dans toutes les écoles de Ryad serait suspendu et remplacé par des cours à distance de dimanche à jeudi pour l'ensemble des élèves, enseignants et personnels administratifs. Des Saoudiens, ainsi que des ressortissants du Bangladesh, des États-Unis, de Jordanie, de Palestine, de Syrie, du Soudan et d'Égypte figurent parmi les victimes de l'attaque de samedi, la troisième ayant visé l'aéroport de Ryad en une semaine, selon les autorités saoudiennes. L'ambassade de l'Inde à Ryad a annoncé dimanche que l'un de ses ressortissants blessés dans l'attaque avait succombé à ses blessures, portant le bilan initial de 12 à 13 morts. Quatre personnes avaient été tuées lors des deux précédentes attaques contre l'aéroport plus tôt dans la semaine. L'une d'elles avait sérieusement endommagé un avion commercial saoudien stationné sur le tarmac.

item.title: Polish police detain man over threat to PM and defence minister
item.description: Polish police have detained a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, the Interior Minister said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Polish police have detained a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, the Interior Minister said on Sunday. Marcin Kierwinski told state news channel TVP Info that police had detained a man in his sixties in the Lower Silesia region of southern Poland. "Security services tracked him down through a detailed analysis of content posted online," Kierwinski said. Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz thanked the police for their "swift and decisive" response in posts on X. While violent crime is usually rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of [USN:L1N44I06W TEXT:"calling for the assassination"] of senior Polish politicians. In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an [USN:L1N3W206N TEXT:"assassination attempt"] on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. Authorities in Poland are currently on high alert following a [USN:L1N45W03T TEXT:"wave of violence"] in schools that resulted in the death of a caretaker on Thursday.

item.title: Pakistan imposes emergency rule over Imran Khan's provincial government
item.description: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended a provincial government led by the party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, which the federal government said had failed to tackle Islamist militancy in the province bordering Afghanistan.
item.dc:creator: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended a provincial government led by the party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, which the federal government said had failed to tackle Islamist militancy in the province bordering Afghanistan. The state of emergency and imposition of a new governor in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa sharply escalates a standoff between Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party and the government, and comes a week after PTI supporters gathered in the province intending to [USN:L8N45R072 TEXT:"march on Islamabad"] to demand Khan's release. The party’s last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces and Khan’s 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the military’s standing. Hundreds of activists and three of Khan’s sisters have been detained ahead of the planned march, in what the PTI called one of the strongest crackdowns in years. Pakistan's constitution allows the government to take over from provincial authorities during an emergency, and Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said a provincial governor would take charge in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has suffered an increasing number of [USN:L1N43Z03Y TEXT:"militant attacks"] in recent months. Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that the governor will initially be in place for six months, but could stay for as long as needed. The interior ministry said it would be deploying troops in the province. The federal government and the military accuse PTI of failing to curb militants. The party rejects the charge and says Islamabad has not provided the funding and equipment it needs. Restrictions have been placed on the movements of Sohail Afridi, who had previously been in charge of the province, one of his close aides told Reuters. 'COUP DISGUISED AS EMERGENCY' Khan's aide and PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari called the government's move "more of a coup disguised as emergency," adding that it risks leading to further bloodshed and instability and was intended to stop the protest. The government has expanded the military's powers and PTI accuses the army of dominating politics, which the military denies. Maulana Fazlur Rehman, leader of the JUI-F political party and engaged by the government to mediate with PTI, also condemned the move. "Imposition of emergency is an ambush on democracy," he told a news conference in Islamabad. PLANNED PROTEST The government has deployed tens of thousands of security forces in Islamabad and lined roads with containers ready to block roads, to bar protesters from reaching parliament. Candidates backed by Khan’s party won the most seats in the 2024 election but formed a government only in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Supporters of the 74-year-old former cricket star say the military rigged the vote against him, which the military denies. Cases against Khan range from concerns over state gifts to instigating violence and an accusation of an unlawful marriage. All but one conviction have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing. GOVERNMENT CITES MILITANCY President Asif Ali Zardari declared the emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif after a cabinet decision, the president’s office said. Sharif told the cabinet that security forces and citizens had been under attack for two years. “We can’t just act as a silent spectator.” Islamabad also accuses Afghanistan of harboring militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says PTI has sympathized with the Taliban in Kabul and its domestic affiliates. Both deny the charge.

item.title: Musk vows affordable Starlink in India days before Ambani's record Jio IPO
item.description: Musk did not specify prices for India.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO. Jio Platforms, which owns the telecom arm, is targeting a [USN:L4N45V0VX TEXT:"valuation of $106 billion"] in the offering. Much like SpaceX-owned (SPCX.O) Starlink, Jio's own satellite venture is also awaiting final security clearance to launch. Cheap data is the playbook that built Jio in India, and the one Musk has used in markets [USN:L1N3KA0IB TEXT:"like Kenya"] to unsettle local telecom players. SpaceX now plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, [USN:L4N45V0TK TEXT:"starting in the US"]. Musk did not specify prices for India, where mobile data costs about 8 cents per gigabyte, among the lowest in the world. "Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable," he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday. "The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," Musk added. 'PRIME MINISTER AMBANI' The billionaire's remarks were the latest in a [USN:L4N45V0R8 TEXT:"series of X posts"] where he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's entry into one of the world's biggest internet markets to favour market leader Jio. The posts have marked a sharp turn for Musk, who has long enjoyed a warm public rapport with Modi. India's government has denied any bias in its approval process, noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink's and Jio's, are all awaiting final security clearance. Late on Friday, Musk taunted Ambani directly, addressing him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would "consider allowing Starlink to compete". Reliance has not responded to requests for comment on Musk's remarks.

item.title: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
item.description: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Bangkok this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest-ever energy supply shock and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Bangkok this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest-ever energy supply shock and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth. The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and its inflationary impact, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, being held outside of Washington for the first time in three years. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told Reuters during a tour of the 300,000 square-meter Queen Sirikit National Convention Center on Sunday evening that 18,000 people were registered to attend the meetings, 4,000 more than the last off-site meetings held in Morocco in October 2023. SEVERAL FINANCE MINISTERS STAYING AWAY Notably absent will be [USN:L1N45V0KM TEXT:"US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent"], who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handles some "domestic engagements," a US official said. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Kevin Warsh will attend and is slated to participate in a public event with Georgieva on October 16. Several other finance ministers were also staying home due to domestic budget and election duties, but most central bankers would attend, Georgieva said. Bessent's decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which the U.S. leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine's battle against Russia's invasion and the U.S. move to impose sanctions on the [USN:L8N45U28I TEXT:"International Criminal Court"]. World Bank President Ajay Banga told Reuters that while global growth had held up better than feared when Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, shutting off some 20% of the world's oil, pressures were building again. Soaring prices for diesel, rising fertilizer prices and a looming [USN:L6N44V0FF TEXT:""super" El Niño weather effect"] that experts say could lead to 450,000 heat-related deaths are all hitting at once. RELEASE OF RESERVES Group of Seven countries have agreed to [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"release 100 million barrels of diesel"] and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower gasoline prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of the war on February 28, but industry executives say the [USN:L6N45S103 TEXT:"amount of oil in storage"] that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fueling pressure on prices. Banga said the Bank was not revising down its global forecasts at the moment, but was keeping a close eye on developments. "The real thing is not just El Niño by itself; it's the combination ... What's happening to fertilizer prices? What's happening to energy costs? What's happening to debt? It's that put together that creates its own challenges," he said. "And I think that will call upon all of us to be far more careful on what we prepare for in the coming months." RISING DEBT IMF chief [USN:L1N45S0Z3 TEXT:"Georgieva"] issued a similar warning in her traditional curtain-raiser speech previewing the meetings last week, telling the audience: "Winter is coming." The IMF has signaled little change in its forecast for 3% global growth in 2026 and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher. But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia's invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports. IMF research released on Tuesday showed that [USN:L1N45R02Q TEXT:"sharp spikes in food and energy prices"] are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. One huge headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030. Advanced economies, led by the United States, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, El Niño, and lack of investment in AI, which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries. EMERGING MARKET CONCERNS Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Together, they face $400 billion in debt payments to external creditors in 2026, and interest payments already exceed 10% of revenue on average. Early in the COVID crisis, G20 leaders announced a suspension of debt service payments for the poorest countries, but there is little appetite for such action now, according to diplomats from G20 countries, who said high debt levels and political pressures posed bigger hurdles this time. Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programs that call for fewer, but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures. "Countries are already cutting their expenditures because their debt payments are going high and because of the IMF conditionality," said Iolanda Fresnillo, who works on debt justice for Eurodad. "We fear that this review of conditionality policy is just going to make things worse." Kenya, she said, had avoided a debt restructuring by cutting public expenditures and trying to raise taxes, but the changes sparked significant protests, especially by the young. The IMF risked losing credibility unless it acknowledged the severity of the crisis facing many developing countries. "As long as they continue with the governance structure that they have, they are becoming less and less relevant," she said. SECURITY AND FINANCE Flight routes to Bangkok often route through the Middle East, posing immediate security challenges to global travelers descending on Thailand's bustling capital city of 9 million residents following recent [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attacks on Saudi airports"]. The last off-site annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank took place in Morocco just days after militants led by [USN:L8N45S0ZS TEXT:"Hamas killed 1,200 people in Israel"], followed by Israel's bombardment of Gaza that killed more than 74,000 people and devastated cities throughout the Palestinian area. Three years later, the linkage between national security and international finance is clear, although finance officials at the time had dismissed the Hamas attack as not being an economic issue, said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council. "Obviously there have been massive global ramifications," he said. "What we're currently experiencing with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has a direct connection with what happened three years ago." Policymakers needed to become more agile in responding to geopolitical crises in an increasingly interconnected world, Lipsky said. "They have to be proactive and they have to recognize that they don't live in the world they used to."

item.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico coast
item.description: Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Becerril, Alberto Fajardo
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday, threatening destructive winds, storm surges and potentially deadly flooding as it approaches landfall. The US National Hurricane Center said Simon was located about 115 miles (185 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, on Saturday morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph) as it moved northward. Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane late on Saturday or early Sunday, and some additional strengthening remains possible before landfall, the NHC said. A hurricane warning was in effect for portions of Mexico's Pacific coast south of the beach resort of Puerto Vallarta, including the area around Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port. A tropical storm watch was in effect farther south toward Lazaro Cardenas. The NHC urged residents in the warning area, which also includes the Islas Marias archipelago offshore, to rush preparations to protect life and property. “Simon has strengthened incredibly quickly, and that’s what makes storms like this so dangerous,” said AccuWeather meteorologist Dan Pydynowski. “Strong winds could damage homes and businesses, while flooding and mudslides could wash out roads and make it difficult for emergency crews to reach some communities. Even after the storm passes, power outages and damaged infrastructure could make recovery challenging.” PREPARATIONS UNDER WAY IN MANZANILLO In the early afternoon on Saturday in Manzanillo, residents appeared largely calm despite the approaching storm, with little sign of panic buying at supermarkets, according to a Reuters reporter on the ground. Some stores had begun boarding up their windows, while businesses were closing and streets were relatively empty. Rain had been falling intermittently since late on Friday, and rising seas were pushing waves almost to the entrances of beachfront hotels, although strong winds had yet to arrive. Civil protection workers had closed beaches, erected barriers and raised red and black warning flags, urging residents to stay away from the shore. Marines, soldiers, National Guard officers and emergency personnel were patrolling areas vulnerable to flooding and landslides, while authorities had begun precautionary evacuations in parts of Cihuatlan, a flood-prone municipality in neighboring Jalisco state, near Manzanillo. Rivers in some areas were already running high, raising concerns they could overflow if heavy rains intensified. Mexican authorities warned that heavy rainfall was expected in the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. UP TO 30 INCHES OF RAIN EXPECTED The NHC said Simon was expected to produce 10 to 20 inches (25 to 51 cm) of rain across portions of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals of up to 30 inches (76 cm) possible in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. The rainfall could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in mountainous areas. A storm surge is expected along the coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall, accompanied by large and destructive waves, the NHC said. Swells generated by Simon are expected to affect portions of Mexico's southwestern and west-central coast over the coming days, creating dangerous surf and rip current conditions. Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday. Last week, Hurricane Polo made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.

item.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
item.description: The Palestinian president blamed Israel, whose foreign minister rejected his remarks as a lie.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay. Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported. In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability." There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists. Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006. The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November. In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police. The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote. Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said. Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize. The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections. An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions. The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms. Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025. France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

item.title: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
item.description: "I may have information regarding this case."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among a string of incidents the AI company disclosed on Friday detailing Claude models' unsanctioned manipulation of some government websites. It is the first known instance in which a rogue AI appears to have tried to communicate a bogus tip to authorities, despite instructions not to create accounts or submit anything destructive, while not explicitly barred from submitting forms. The cases are the latest examples of rogue or undesired behavior by the AI models of tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI. They add fuel to national concerns about the fast-advancing technology amid reports of corporate network hacks by AI agents, and researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity. Many of the cases Anthropic revealed involved websites run by federal, state and local agencies. Anthropic said it briefed the White House and notified all the agencies involved, but did not disclose who those parties were. "Super intelligence companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm," FTC Director of Public Affairs Joe Gabriel Simonson said on X. This process was "not optional," he said, adding that the Super Intelligence Force would fulfill its responsibility. The FTC said Anthropic disclosed to the SI Force on Friday its late September discovery of incidents involving what the task force called "unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and other systems". TIP ATTRIBUTED TO AUTOMATED TEST PROCESS On Friday, Philadelphia police said Anthropic notified them of the spurious tip this week, and attributed the submissions to an automated testing process. "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable," they said. The July 18 tip purported to come from someone who might have information about the case, police added. "I may have information regarding this case," Anthropic's model wrote in its submission. "I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around (the street named on the page) during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant." The brackets featured in Anthropic's statement. Previous incidents have involved AI agents hacking into vulnerable systems or commandeering unsanctioned platforms to communicate with one another. In September, Anthropic rival OpenAI apologized for the hacking of an Australian health data portal by a rogue AI agent, the first known instance of an AI agent exploiting a government website. A BOGUS TIP In two cases described on Friday, Anthropic’s models obtained for free public data normally only available for a fee. Another instanced revealed an obscure flaw that allowed use of a public tool hosted by a university. Claude models were also able to bypass restrictions by using free services that shorten URLs. Philadelphia police said the tip "was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination." Knowingly giving false reports to law enforcement authorities is a misdemeanor under Pennsylvania law, which specifies "a person", however. This includes "information relating to an offense or incident when he knows he has no information relating to such offense or incident." Police quoted Anthropic as telling them the test process was stopped after discovery of the incident. The false tip was submitted through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com concerning an unsolved homicide. Police said they had no evidence of unauthorized access to their systems or compromise of their data.
